q: The Gibbs paradox (entropy of mixing) arises when mixing two volumes of the same ideal gas. The correct resolution (via Gibbs) gives ΔS_mixing = 0 for identical gases because:
opts: Identical particles are indistinguishable; the correct Gibbs entropy uses 1/N! in the partition function (counting distinct microstates)
Mixing doesn't occur for identical gases
exp: Gibbs resolution: dividing the classical partition function by N! (for identical particles) gives the Sackur-Tetrode equation for the entropy, which correctly gives ΔS_mixing = 0 for identical gases and the correct entropy of mixing for distinguishable gases. This is a precursor to quantum statistics.
